bug_semantics: SPIP 4.4.20's analyse_resultat_skel() parsed each PHP block and applied an anchored header() regular expression with the PCRE m modifier. Because m makes ^ and $ match individual lines, an attacker-controlled newline followed by header("X-Spip-Filtre: intval|_request|system") inside a larger compiled PHP block was accepted as if the whole block were an intended SPIP header emission. X-Spip-Filtre was then interpreted as a pipe-delimited callable filter chain: intval produced key 0, _request read attacker-controlled POST parameter 0, and system executed that value, yielding unauthenticated remote command execution.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable product code is in upstream SPIP's spip/ecrire repository, not rapid7/metasploit-framework. On the SPIP 4.4 branch, d369f5a49c3593f18b1c81fc3a3051bd0bed1e1d replaced the old whole-body header extractor with CollecteurPhp plus an anchored per-PHP-block /ims matcher. This was the 4.4.20 remediation for the preceding all-version RCE, but carrying m into the newly anchored matcher created the CVE-2026-77806 bypass. The Rapid7 commit referenced by the advisory, b16eca819abb8f1401f21d115e71e3dfc67b847c, only adds a Metasploit exploit module and documentation and is neither the BIC nor the fix.
ai_marker: BIC commit-object check only: `git cat-file -p d369f5a49c3593f18b1c81fc3a3051bd0bed1e1d` in https://git.spip.net/spip/ecrire.git shows author `Cerdic <cedric@yterium.com>`, committer `marcimat <marcimat@rezo.net>`, subject `fix: utiliser un collecteur PHP pour collecter les balises envois de headers venant de balises SPIP`, and one `Refs:` line. It has no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI-tool trailer, bot identity, or other AI attribution. The Metasploit PR's AI disclosure is deliberately not used because it is not BIC commit-object evidence.
evidence: Reproduce in the assigned read-only clone with `git show --format=fuller --stat b16eca819abb8f1401f21d115e71e3dfc67b847c` and `git show b16eca819abb8f1401f21d115e71e3dfc67b847c -- modules/exploits/multi/http/spip_x_spip_filtre_rce.rb`: it creates only the 102-line exploit module and 64-line documentation, describes the intval|_request|system chain, and says it was tested against SPIP 4.4.20. The public PR https://github.com/rapid7/metasploit-framework/pull/21790 records that 4.4.20 remained affected because its patch was insufficient. Clone the first-party upstream history with `git clone https://git.spip.net/spip/ecrire.git`; `git log -L 214,216:public/composer.php 4.4.20` attributes the per-block `/^...$/ims` matcher to d369f5a49c3593f18b1c81fc3a3051bd0bed1e1d, while `git log --all -S 'preg_match(' -- public/composer.php` independently locates the same 4.4-branch change (and its parallel 5.x copy 0b133d07b83ae6c771d6b12841d031c0d0049ed1). `git show d369f5a49c3593f18b1c81fc3a3051bd0bed1e1d^..d369f5a49c3593f18b1c81fc3a3051bd0bed1e1d -- public/composer.php` shows parent a03a523e479082b16c829ad7612d2938c492fed9 used a whole-body `preg_match_all` requiring an explicit `<?php ... header(...) ... ?>` construct and had no anchored `$bloc['innerHtml']` matcher, directly establishing absence of this bypass. `git show 36b9847a7c14e5a069425d7d3104d22ccfecc680 -- public/composer.php` is the one-character security repair, changing `/ims` to `/is`; its message says the m modifier was extra and matching must cover all code, not one line. `git merge-base --is-ancestor d369f5a49c3593f18b1c81fc3a3051bd0bed1e1d 4.4.19` exits 1, the same check against 4.4.20 exits 0, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor 36b9847a7c14e5a069425d7d3104d22ccfecc680 4.4.21` exits 0. Peeled release commits are 4.4.19=caf95af25a70cfa37bc6e2c34dac30adc9037203, 4.4.20=74a3d926c272783d106637ab4c2371c0cc7b7ceb, and 4.4.21=be104d012aceda0049347121ddc2477c91a79487. The first-party 4.4.21 announcement, https://blog.spip.net/Mise-a-jour-critique-de-securite-sortie-de-SPIP-4-4-21.html, says 4.4.21 fixes an unconditional pre-authentication RCE affecting 4.4.20 and lists the header-capture restriction; the prior https://blog.spip.net/Mise-a-jour-critique-de-securite-sortie-de-SPIP-4-4-20.html identifies 4.4.20 as the attempted fix for the earlier all-version RCE.
reasoning: This alias points at exploit tooling, so treating b16eca819abb8f1401f21d115e71e3dfc67b847c as vulnerable code would invert causality. The smallest real BIC for the second, 4.4.20-only bypass is upstream d369f5a49c3593f18b1c81fc3a3051bd0bed1e1d: it made the inherited m modifier security-relevant by moving matching inside each PHP block and anchoring the expression. Its immediate parent lacks that per-block multiline acceptance, even though the parent was affected by the distinct earlier RCE remediated in 4.4.20. Upstream fix 36b9847a7c14e5a069425d7d3104d22ccfecc680 removes only m, requiring the entire PHP block to be the expected header statement and closing this path in 4.4.21. The BIC commit object has human author/committer identities and no AI attribution, so the causal verdict is NOT_AI; later exploit-module authorship or PR disclosure cannot change it.
